cards.subject: The LAST attached card is the Elevation of the Host from this same set and shows this same Mass. Paint the SAME church and the same sanctuary: the same white-and-gold high altar with its gradines, six tall lit candles, crucifix, three altar cards and white-veiled tabernacle, the same priest in the same white-and-gold Roman fiddleback chasuble with maniple over a lace alb, the same servers in cassock and lace surplice, the same thurifer and the same four torchbearers, each in the same place, so that the cards read as one sequence. This card is the moment BEFORE that elevation, the Consecration of the Host, seen from the same foot of the altar steps but a few paces to the right, so that the priest is seen from behind and from his right side and his hands show beyond his arm. The priest bows low over the altar, his forearms resting on it, his head inclined, holding the large white Host just above the white corporal between the thumbs and forefingers of both hands, his eyes on it, saying the words of consecration in silence; beside it on the corporal stands the golden chalice covered with its white pall. No one lifts the chasuble and no bell rings: the server on the edge of the foot-pace kneels with joined hands, the second server kneels on the step with the small bell resting beside him, the thurifer kneels with the thurible hanging still on its chains, a thin thread of smoke rising, and the four torchbearers kneel in a line holding their tall lit torches. At the very bottom of the arch, the heads and shoulders of the faithful kneeling at the altar rail, seen from behind, the women veiled. Figures small in the scene. Hushed, breathless, hidden. Keep everything inside the pointed arch. The card's frame is exactly the attached cards': the coloured initial box at the top-left, one vine-and-flower band to its right along the top and one along the bottom, plain parchment margins down the sides, and the arched window ending ABOVE the bottom band.
cards.frame: the inner window is a POINTED GOTHIC ARCH with slender gold tracery at its tip, like a sanctuary seen through a church arch; no halo
cards.basis: The priest 'cubitis super Altare positis, stans capite inclinato, distincte, reverenter et secreto profert verba consecrationis' over the Host, which he holds 'pollicibus et indicibus' (Ritus servandus VIII.5); 'he now bows over the altar, leaning the forearms on it' (Fortescue, l. 4871–4874). The chalice is still covered. The server lifts the chasuble and rings only at the elevations (VIII.6; Fortescue, l. 6384–6390, 6403), the thurifer incenses only then (VIII.8), and the torches are held from the Sanctus (Fortescue, l. 9613–9617).

cards.subject: The Elevation of the Host at a sung Mass, seen straight on from the foot of the altar steps, the altar the centre. At a white-and-gold high altar with gradines, six tall lit candles, a crucifix, the three altar cards and the tabernacle veiled in white, the priest, in a white-and-gold Roman fiddleback chasuble with the maniple on his left arm, over an amice and a lace-trimmed alb, seen from behind, facing the altar, raises the white Host high above his head with both hands. Behind him, kneeling on the edge of the foot-pace, a server in cassock and white lace surplice lifts the hem of the chasuble with one hand; on the step at the right a second server kneels and rings a small bell; at the side a kneeling thurifer swings a smoking thurible toward the Host; four torchbearers kneel in a line across the sanctuary floor, holding tall lit torches. Soft golden rays fall from above onto the Host. At the very bottom of the arch, the heads and shoulders of the faithful kneeling at the altar rail, seen from behind, the women veiled. Figures small in the scene. Adoring, still. Keep everything inside the pointed arch. The card's frame is exactly the attached cards': the coloured initial box at the top-left, one vine-and-flower band to its right along the top and one along the bottom, plain parchment margins down the sides, and the arched window ending ABOVE the bottom band.
cards.frame: the inner window is a POINTED GOTHIC ARCH with slender gold tracery at its tip, like a sanctuary seen through a church arch; no halo
cards.basis: After the words of consecration the priest genuflects, then 'elevat in altum Hostiam, et intentis in eam oculis populo reverenter ostendit adorandam' (Ritus servandus VIII.5). Meanwhile the server 'manu sinistra elevat fimbrias posteriores Planetae, ne ipsum Celebrantem impediat in elevatione brachiorum … et manu dextera pulsat campanulam ter ad unamquamque elevationem' (VIII.6); the thurifer, kneeling, incenses the Host three times (VIII.8; Fortescue, l. 9949–9962). The picture is the Consecration card of batch 47, with its initial changed from C to E.

This card is the Consecration of the Chalice: the priest bows low over the altar, his forearms resting on it, his head inclined, holding the uncovered golden CHALICE a little raised above the white corporal with both hands, his right hand at its knob and his left under its foot, his eyes on it, saying the words of consecration in silence; before the chalice the consecrated white Host lies on the corporal, and the white pall lies to one side. No one lifts the chasuble and no bell rings: the server on the edge of the foot-pace kneels with joined hands, the second server kneels on the step with the small bell resting beside him, the thurifer kneels with the thurible hanging still on its chains, a thin thread of smoke rising, and the four torchbearers kneel in a line holding their tall lit torches. At the very bottom of the arch, the heads and shoulders of the faithful kneeling at the altar rail, seen from behind, the women veiled. Figures small in the scene. Hushed, breathless, hidden. Keep everything inside the pointed arch. The card's frame is exactly the attached cards': the coloured initial box at the top-left, one vine-and-flower band to its right along the top and one along the bottom, plain parchment margins down the sides, and the arched window ending ABOVE the bottom band.

cards.basis: The priest holds the chalice 'ambabus manibus … videlicet sinistra pedem, dextera nodum infra cuppam, cubitis super Altare positis, et capite inclinato, profert attente, continuate et secreto … verba consecrationis Sanguinis', 'tenens illum parum elevatum' (Ritus servandus VIII.7; DO Latin Ordo; Fortescue, l. 4945–4953). The Host has been laid back on the corporal (VIII.5). The server lifts the chasuble and rings only at the elevations (VIII.6).

cards.basis: Having said Haec quotiescumque the priest genuflects, then, 'accipiens Calicem discoopertum cum Sanguine ambabus manibus, ut prius, elevat eum, et erectum quantum commode potest, ostendit populo adorandum' (Ritus servandus VIII.7). The server lifts the chasuble and rings as at the Host, 'quod et facit in elevatione Calicis' (VIII.6), and the thurifer incenses 'similiter Calicem' (VIII.8). The Mystery of Faith card shows the same elevation from among the people.
